newsitem.title: USA: United Meridian has dry holes.
newsitem.headline: United Meridian has dry holes.

text.p: United Meridian Corp said Tuesday the Perla 1, the company's first well drilled on its 75 percent owned, 190,000-acre Block D offshore Equatorial Guinea, has been abandoned after reaching a total depth of 9,575 feet.

Offshore the Ivory Coast, the company said, the Simba 1 well on its 25 percent-owned Block CI-11 encountered 200 feet of Cenomanian sand with oil shows but held no commercial potential. The deeper, primary objective, the Lion sands, were present but not hydrocarbon-bearing.

It said the Perla 1, located about 15 miles northeast of UMC's 25 percent owned Zafiro field on Block B, found multiple reservoir quality sands in the shallower secondary objective interval, but they contained only residual hydrocarbons.

In the deeper primary interval, targeted sands in the lower Qua Iboe formation, which were encountered in a well drilled by a major oil company in 1968 about 2.5 miles west of Perla 1, were not present in the Perla well.

The rig that drilled the Perla 1, the Adriatic X, will immediately move to drill UMC's second prospect on Block D, the Tsavorita 1, located about 12 miles northeast of the Perla well, the company said.

The well is sited four miles southwest of the Moudi field in Cameroon, which is oil productive from Qua Iboe sands. Located in 100 feet of water, the Tsavorita is expected to reach its proposed total depth of 8,800 feet by mid-February.

It said the Adriatic IV rig that drilled the Simba prospect moved 75 miles east and began drilling the Kudu 1, a 9,000-foot exploratory well on Block CI-01 in the easternmost part of Ivory Coast on December 31. The Kudu 1 is located l.5 miles northeast of a well drilled by a major oil company in the mid-80s, which tested 39 million cubic feet of natural gas and 1,200 barrels of oil per day. Results are expected by February 1. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
